name: Persistent Surveillance and Termination Drone PSTD-1 'Shepherd'
description: The PSTD-1 is a single-target autonomous pursuit drone designed not for immediate lethality but for indefinite surveillance and conditional termination. Roughly the size of a clenched fist, the Shepherd locks onto a biometric profile—gait signature, thermal pattern, or facial geometry—and maintains persistent tracking at distances of up to 1.2 kilometers, hovering at rooftop altitude and transmitting encrypted telemetry to its registered operator. It carries a single-shot linear magnetically accelerated flechette, 4.5mm tungsten-core, capable of killing an unarmored human target at 300 meters. The shot is only fired upon explicit operator command or upon activation of a conditional trigger pre-programmed at deployment.
legality: Licensed — conditional termination trigger requires Class-7 Autonomous Lethality Permit; unlocked units Prohibited
specifications:
dimensions: 112mm x 98mm x 76mm
mass: 340 grams
tracking range: 1.2km (surveillance mode), 300m (termination envelope)
endurance: Up to 72 hours (surveillance mode), 11 hours (active stalk mode)
payload: Single 4.5mm tungsten-core flechette, linear magnetic launch
muzzle velocity: 920 m/s
biometric lock time: 4.2 seconds initial acquisition
re-acquisition after loss: Up to 22 minutes lost contact before profile reset
operator interface: Encrypted short-range telemetry uplink, compatible with standard AR overlays
self-destruct: Thermite core (operator-triggered or tamper-activated)
tactical_use: Corporate collections agencies and high-end enforcement syndicates use the Shepherd to enforce debt, contract, or territorial compliance without committing personnel. A single operator can manage up to six simultaneously deployed units via AR overlay. Conditional triggers are commonly set to location-based parameters—'fire if target enters District 7' or 'fire if target contacts [named individual]'—making the Shepherd a tool for controlling behavior as much as ending lives. Counter-measures include signal-blocking canopies, thermal masking suits (see: TSI-2 'Cold Case'), and the controversial but effective tactic of feeding the drone a spoofed biometric signature to exhaust its battery on a false target.
cultural_context: The Shepherd has become a symbol of corporate reach in GLMZ—the idea that debt and consequence have no geographic limit. ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's marketing language ('consequence enforcement') has entered common parlance as a euphemism for sanctioned killing, and the phrase 'you've been shepherded' carries a specific, chilling meaning in street vernacular. Among mid-level corporate employees, deployment of a Shepherd against a contractor who failed to deliver is considered a proportionate business response, a normalization that civil rights organizations in the city have repeatedly and unsuccessfully challenged.
known_users: Paranoid mid-tier syndicate leaders (deployed against suspected defectors)
story_hooks: A player character discovers a Shepherd has been tailing them for 11 days. The registered operator is listed as a shell corporation that dissolved 6 days ago. The conditional trigger is unknown—and the drone is still active.

A ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC technician is selling unlocked conditional trigger firmware on the black market. The buyers include at least one person who has already used it. Finding the technician before corporate internal security does is worth a significant payout.

A target the party has been hired to protect is convinced a Shepherd is overhead—but all scans come back negative. Is the paranoia the weapon, or is the drone simply better at hiding than its spec sheet suggests?

The party is offered a job: retrieve a decommissioned Shepherd from a sealed evidence locker at an MMPD substation. The drone inside still has its biometric lock active—and the profile it's locked to belongs to a sitting city councilor.
related_entities: Tethered Orbital Reconnaissance and Suppression Drone TORSD-7 'Kitestring'

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, aggressively angular hovering platform resembling a predatory insect in profile—four stabilizer fins arranged in a cross formation with a pronounced conical nose section. The overall aesthetic is brutalist and utilitarian, with minimal ornamentation. At rest, it sits like a clenched fist-sized stone, deceptively inert.
physical_description.dimensions: 112mm length (nose to tail boom), 98mm fin-span (wingtip to wingtip), 76mm vertical profile; flechette barrel is recessed and unobtrusive, flush with the nose cone
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively dense—340 grams feels heavier in palm than its size suggests. Balanced around the central thrust axis, though the magnetic payload adds subtle weight-forward bias. Feels like holding a loaded piece of industrial machinery.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade carbon composite chassis with embedded kinetic harvesting micro-turbine housing; tungsten-core flechette payload in magnetic launch tube (internal)
physical_description.finish: Matte anthracite with a subtle brushed texture across flight surfaces to minimize reflectivity. Launch tube collar shows light polishing wear. Overall deliberately non-reflective to avoid optical detection.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with accent striping in deep infrared-spectrum black along stabilizer edges. Minimal branding—only a small etched ZHENG-DAO cipher on the tail boom, intentionally dull.
physical_description.grip_texture: Not designed for hand-carry; charging/maintenance contacts are smooth ceramic-polymer. When held for inspection, the fuselage has a slightly textured, non-slip micro-finish.
distinctive_features: Recessed magnetic launch aperture disguised as aerodynamic nose fairing
Four cruciform stabilizer fins with subtle leading-edge vanes for directional micro-adjustments
Kinetic turbine intake vents along the flanks (appear as subtle horizontal slots)
Thermal management grilles visible beneath the rear boom section
AR-compatible telemetry antenna (nearly invisible, integrated into tail spike)
Thermite self-destruct core housing creates an almost imperceptible weight asymmetry at the rear
Biometric sensor cluster (LWIR + visual) housed in a small dark dome on the dorsal surface
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC logo etched in 8pt font on starboard tail boom; Class-7 permit stamp (if licensed) appears as a laser-etched serial identifier on the maintenance access plate. Black-market units have this plate either removed or crudely defaced.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show minimal cosmetic wear despite heavy use—dirt residue on sensor dome, micro-scratches on fin leading edges from rooftop navigation, occasional carbon scoring around the launch aperture. Licensed corporate units are meticulously maintained. Black-market units often show signs of field repair: mismatched patch panels, corroded antenna housings, tape-wrapped micro-fractures.
